subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: GI neuroendocrine tumours and the gut in systemic disease

steps.tx: A **24-hour** urine collection for **5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid**, or **5-HIAA**, is the biochemical test for carcinoid syndrome. The patient must avoid tryptophan-rich foods during the collection, including bananas, avocados and walnuts, or the result is falsely high. The drawing shows why the syndrome needs liver metastases: the liver normally clears the mediators. A high 5-HIAA with flushing is the classic pair. One random blood serotonin is not this test.
steps.say: Collect a 24-hour urine for 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid, also called 5-HIAA, when you suspect carcinoid syndrome. Bananas, avocados and walnuts during the collection cause a false rise. The syndrome needs mediators to escape the liver.

vis.alt: Liver deposits let mediators bypass the liver, with flushing, diarrhoea and right-sided valve thickening.
vis.caption: Carcinoid syndrome when hepatic clearance is bypassed. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **177Lu-dotatate** is peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. It delivers beta radiation to well-differentiated midgut neuroendocrine tumours that still carry somatostatin receptors. The **NETTER-1 trial** showed longer progression-free survival with this treatment. The digits are 177 in the isotope and 1 in the trial name. It is for receptor-positive disease. A tumour that has lost the receptor will not take up the isotope.
steps.say: 177Lu-dotatate is peptide receptor radiotherapy for receptor-positive well-differentiated midgut neuroendocrine tumours. The NETTER-1 trial showed longer progression-free survival. A tumour without the receptor is not a candidate.

rows: Receptor lost, isotope will not bind

steps.tx: A **VIPoma** is a pancreatic tumour that secretes vasoactive intestinal peptide. The clinical name is **WDHA syndrome**: watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia and achlorhydria. The diarrhoea is secretory, so it continues when the patient stops eating. Potassium losses are large. Look in the pancreas when a secretory diarrhoea has no infection. It is not carcinoid syndrome, which flushes and raises 5-HIAA.
steps.say: VIPoma causes WDHA syndrome: watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia and achlorhydria. The diarrhoea continues during fasting because it is secretory. Potassium falls hard, and this is not carcinoid syndrome.

steps.tx: **Glucagonoma** is an alpha-cell pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour. The skin clue is **necrolytic migratory erythema**, a spreading rash that blisters and scales. Patients also have mild diabetes, a normocytic anaemia and a tendency to deep vein thrombosis. The drawing shows the pancreatic tail mass and the rash. A chronic odd rash plus diabetes and weight loss should make you measure glucagon and image the pancreas.
steps.say: Glucagonoma presents with necrolytic migratory erythema, mild diabetes, anaemia and thrombosis. The tumour is an alpha-cell mass, often in the pancreatic tail. A strange migrating rash plus diabetes deserves a glucagon level.

vis.alt: A pancreatic tail tumour with migratory scaling plaques and superficial epidermal necrolysis.
vis.caption: Necrolytic migratory erythema of glucagonoma. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Systemic sclerosis** affects the gut after the nerves fail and the smooth muscle atrophies and fibroses. The oesophagus stops peristalsis. The colon develops **wide-mouthed diverticula**. The small bowel can pseudo-obstruct. Reflux and bacterial overgrowth follow the dysmotility. Proton pump treatment and antibiotics for overgrowth are supportive. The diverticula are wide-mouthed, unlike ordinary colonic diverticula, and that shape is the exam point.
steps.say: Systemic sclerosis starts with nerve failure, then muscle atrophy and fibrosis. You should expect an aperistaltic oesophagus, wide-mouthed diverticula and pseudo-obstruction. Reflux and bacterial overgrowth are treated as support. The wide mouth of the diverticulum is the finding to name.

steps.tx: **Gastrointestinal amyloidosis** causes dysmotility, malabsorption and a large tongue. The deposit is extracellular and amorphous. Under polarised light after Congo red it shows **apple-green birefringence**, which is the pathognomonic look. The micrograph is that green shine around tissue structures. Macroglossia plus diarrhoea or a bleed should make you stain for amyloid. Do not call it inflammatory bowel disease because the colon looks a bit red.
steps.say: Gastrointestinal amyloidosis causes dysmotility, malabsorption and macroglossia. Congo red under polarised light gives apple-green birefringence. That shine is the diagnosis, and you should not mistake it for ordinary colitis.

vis.alt: Green-gold birefringence around tissue structures under polarised light.
vis.caption: Apple-green birefringence of amyloid. Image: Ed Uthman, CC BY, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Acute intestinal **graft-versus-host disease** causes large volumes of green watery diarrhoea, cramps and a denuded mucosa. Grading uses **stool volume**. **Grade 1** is more than **500** mL a day. **Grade 4** is more than **1500** mL a day. The drawing shows donor lymphocytes, crypt injury and a sloughed intestinal lining. Stool infection must be excluded, but volume this high after a transplant is GVHD until proved otherwise.
steps.say: Acute graft-versus-host disease of the gut causes green watery diarrhoea. Grade 1 is stool volume above 500 millilitres a day. Grade 4 is above 1500 millilitres a day. The mucosa sloughs, so you should exclude infection and then treat the graft-versus-host disease.

vis.alt: Donor lymphocytes damaging skin, bile duct and intestinal mucosa, with crypt injury and sloughing.
vis.caption: Acute graft-versus-host disease in skin, liver and gut. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Checkpoint inhibitor enterocolitis** follows anti-CTLA-4 drugs, especially **ipilimumab**, and also anti-PD-1 drugs. The digit 4 is in CTLA-4 and the digit 1 is in PD-1. Patients get severe watery diarrhoea and mucosal ulcers. High-dose corticosteroids are first treatment. If steroids fail, give infliximab or vedolizumab early rather than waiting out a long steroid course. Hold the immunotherapy. This is not infection until you have looked, but do not delay the steroid while cultures cook if the patient is toxic.
steps.say: Checkpoint inhibitor enterocolitis, from ipilimumab or an anti-PD-1 drug, causes severe diarrhoea and ulcers. Start high-dose corticosteroids, and if they fail you should add infliximab or vedolizumab early and hold the immunotherapy.

right.title: If steroids fail
points: Do not wait for a long steroid taper.
